_comment: Session config for a document project. It allows the read-only and check commands this work needs, and denies `rm *` for everyone. It is NOT where a contributor's boundary lives -- see _permissions_comment: this file is tracked and repo-wide, while the boundary is .github/CODEOWNERS plus branch protection, per spec/CONTRIBUTOR_ACCESS.md layer 2.
_hooks_comment: THE HOOK SCRIPTS ARE NOT SHIPPED IN THIS TEMPLATE -- copy them, per the
README's instantiation step 3, from templates/harness/claude-code/hooks/
into .claude/hooks/ and make them executable. They live in the harness
adapter rather than here so a fix reaches every adopter through one file
instead of drifting copies (the same reasoning
tools/precedent_bootstrap_source.py's _install_session_hooks() states).
Until 2026-09-10 this file wired session-start.sh and the README never
mentioned templates/harness/ at all, so a verbatim instantiation --
which is exactly what the README's step 2 asks for -- produced a repo
whose SessionStart hook pointed at a file that did not exist, and
tools/bootstrap.sh therefore never ran. Found installing
precedent-beta-v01 into a real project.
WHICH HOOKS, and why these. INSTALL.md §1 step 2's decision table calls
session-start.sh, commit-identity.sh and freshness-guard.sh 'always',
and precedent-paths.sh 'only with the Precedent loader' -- which this
template IS, so it is wired. stop-git-check.sh is the one deliberate
omission, and its reasoning CHANGED on 2026-09-11: it used to be that
the contributor was denied `git push` outright, so the hook would end
every session of theirs in a block they could not clear. They push now
(spec/CONTRIBUTOR_ACCESS.md), and it stays omitted for a smaller
reason -- a document left deliberately unpushed overnight is ordinary
here, and a hook that refuses to end the turn over it is noise.
REPLACE THE BASE BRANCH ARGUMENT (`main` in the three freshness-guard
commands) with this repo's real base branch. It is passed explicitly
because asking git for the default branch gets it wrong in at least one
real repo.
_permissions_comment: WHY THE DENY LIST IS ONE ENTRY. .claude/settings.json is TRACKED, so
it binds every session on this repository and cannot tell one person
from another -- it never sees who is running. Anything role-specific
written here therefore restricts the maintainer exactly as much as the
contributor it was meant for.
This file used to deny `git push`, `git merge`, `git reset` and
`git rebase`, reading spec/CONTRIBUTOR_ACCESS.md's per-person layer
as a repo-wide one. In the template's first real
install (2026-09-10) that cost the repository's own administrator the
ability to push or merge his own work from a session, and the shipped
file's comment had to tell him to edit it before he could land
anything. A default whose first documented step is 'undo this default'
is not a default.
WHERE THE BOUNDARY ACTUALLY LIVES, since 2026-09-11: .github/CODEOWNERS
plus branch protection on the base branch. A pull request touching an
owned path -- the vendored engine, practices/, precedent.json, .claude/,
.github/ -- waits for the maintainer's review; one touching only the
documents is the contributor's to merge. That is a PATH boundary, so it
needs no per-person configuration and nothing has to decide what kind of
person is running. The contributor's own session config still sets the
persona and never sets permission_mode to bypassPermissions.
README.md's instantiation steps 5-7 are those steps;
spec/CONTRIBUTOR_ACCESS.md is the reasoning.
`Bash(rm *)` stays, for everyone, deliberately: it is not
role-specific. Deletion in a document project goes through git, where
it is reviewable and recoverable, and no ordinary work here needs the
shell form.
